title: I can’t wear them if they are grey
html_source:
This recalls Hamlet’s dressing in black and continuing to mourn his father’s death long after the court had stopped (1.2).

At the time the length of mourning (the wearing of black suit and limited social life) would’ve been a year and a day. Stephen is extending it. It is important to note the allusion to Hamlet. Later in Telemachus, Mulligan will state, “It is quite simple. He proves by algebra that Hamlet’s grandson is Shakespeare’s grandfather and that he himself is the ghost of his own father.” Joyce parallels again Christ’s life to Shakespeare to his own biography.
